tasks.description: Extract atomic notes from USV post-processing pipeline research synthesis — hysteresis dual-threshold detection, CNN temperature scaling calibration, PCEN adaptive normalization, two-stage false positive filtering, F-beta scoring for bioacoustic detection, and event-level evaluation methods (collar-based vs IoU)
candidate_claims: No existing mouse USV tool uses explicit hysteresis — all use single-threshold + gap-filling + min-duration
Hysteresis subsumes gap-filling and minimum duration as special cases of dual-threshold logic
DCASE Cances 2019: class-dependent post-processing parameters improved F1 from 37.1% to 43.9%
WhaleVAD-BPN 2024 demonstrates comprehensive hysteresis pipeline for bioacoustic detection
scikit-maad implements double-threshold hysteresis binarization for ecological acoustics
Modern CNNs are systematically miscalibrated (Guo et al., 2017 ICML)
Temperature scaling: single scalar T divides logits before sigmoid — simplest effective calibration
ROC AUC is invariant to temperature scaling (monotonic transformation) but threshold interpretability improves
For small validation sets isotonic regression overfits — prefer temperature scaling
PCEN is gold standard for adaptive normalization in bioacoustic literature (Lostanlen 2019)
BirdVoxDetect PCEN reduced false alarm rates 50x near-field and 5x far-field
PCEN requires retraining — not suitable for current pipeline without model retrain
Clarfeld 2025: secondary logistic regression on features from primary detections 84.5-89.8% accuracy for FP filtering
VocalMat two-stage: morphological filtering + CNN noise classification, >98% detection rate
BootSnap includes explicit false-positive class alongside 11 USV categories
F2 score (beta=2) weights recall ~4x more than precision — standard when FNs are more costly
Collar-based evaluation (±200ms tolerance) better for bioacoustics with uncertain event boundaries
IoU-based evaluation (>=50% overlap) more strict, penalizes fragmented detections

tasks.description: Extract atomic notes from AMVOC deep-read (Stoumpou et al. 2022) — convolutional autoencoder architecture (64×160 input, 8-filter bottleneck, BCE loss), preprocessing pipeline (2ms non-overlapping frames, per-max normalization, zero-pad/center-crop to 64 frames), 4-stage feature post-processing (var threshold→scaler→PCA→t-SNE), clustering methods, hand-crafted baseline comparison (37% improvement for deep features), detection algorithm, and actionable gaps for our wild-mouse VQ-VAE pipeline

source_metadata.paper: Stoumpou et al. (2022). Analysis of Mouse Vocal Communication (AMVOC). Bioacoustics, 32(2), 199–229.

candidate_claims: AMVOC autoencoder uses 64×160 input (128ms × 80kHz range at 0.5kHz resolution) — well-justified for our pipeline
AMVOC encoder bottleneck is 8 filters × 8 × 20 = 1,280 values (8× compression from 10,240 input pixels)
BCE loss with sigmoid output treats each spectrogram pixel as a probability — requires per-max normalization to [0,1]
AMVOC uses per-spectrogram max normalization (divide by max value) — not min-max, not z-score, not log-scale
AMVOC 2ms non-overlapping windows (ST_STEP = ST_WIN) give 0.5 kHz frequency resolution at 30–110 kHz
AMVOC zero-pads short USVs symmetrically and center-crops long USVs to achieve fixed 64 time frames
AMVOC 4-stage feature pipeline: variance thresholding (1,280→~320) → StandardScaler → PCA (95% variance) → t-SNE (visualization only)
AMVOC deep features achieved 37% higher global annotation scores over 4-feature handcrafted baseline (p < 0.01)
AMVOC trained for only 2 epochs deliberately to avoid overfitting — undercomplete bottleneck acts as implicit regularizer
AMVOC lacks batch normalization, dropout, validation monitoring, VAE variant, and UMAP — all improvements for our pipeline
AMVOC code discrepancy: training_task.py uses 8 bottleneck filters (matches paper), conv_autoencoder.py uses 4 filters (may be semi-supervised variant)
AMVOC feature mode 3 (90-dim resampled frequency contour) is architecturally similar to Didi's peak-frequency vectorization

tasks.description: Extract atomic notes from Oren et al. 2024 (Science) deep-read — Omer lab vectorization technique (STFT ridge extraction → 80D FM+AM vector), MATLAB spectrogramming.m pipeline, random forest receiver-ID classification (AUC 0.798), vocal labels evidence, family dialect finding, and Python adaptation notes for mouse USV analysis

source_metadata.paper: Oren, G., Shapira, A., Lifshitz, R., Vinepinsky, E., Cohen, R., Fried, T., Hadad, G.P., & Omer, D. (2024). Vocal labeling of others by nonhuman primates. Science, 385(6712), 996-1003.

candidate_claims: Omer lab vectorization extracts peak frequency per spectrogram column (FM ridge) and amplitude at that ridge (AM) then resamples both to 40 time steps giving an 80-dimensional call vector
MATLAB tfridge extracts the dominant frequency ridge with continuity constraints — Python equivalent is argmax per column with optional smoothness regularization
Omer 2024 spectrogramming.m uses a 50ms Hanning window with 25ms hop and crops to 6-9 kHz before ridge extraction — for mouse USVs window should be ~1ms and range 30-110 kHz
The 80D vector is [AM₁...AM₄₀, FM₁...FM₄₀] where AM is the absolute value of the complex STFT at the ridge position and FM is the frequency value of the ridge
Omer lab normalizes AM and FM independently per caller to [0,1] using rescale — for mouse USVs this would be per-recording or per-mouse normalization
AM features in Omer 2024 are median-smoothed (window=6) and FM features are mean-smoothed (window=5) before concatenation
Omer 2024 random forest receiver-ID classifier achieved average AUC 0.798 across 9 marmoset callers using 150-tree TreeBagger with Random Under-Sampling at 100 calls per class
Omer 2024 leave-one-session-out cross-validation showed no session-specific artifacts (KS test P=0.49) confirming classifier generalizes across sessions
Omer 2024 playback experiment showed monkeys respond with significantly higher probability to calls directed at them versus calls directed at others (Cox regression β=1.39 P < 2.4e-9)
Omer 2024 family dialect analysis using random forest leaf co-occurrence proximity showed within-family calls cluster together even across unrelated adult pairs confirming vocal learning not genetics
Both AM and FM features contribute to receiver-ID classification with AM showing significantly but slightly higher importance (t=5.06 P<0.0001)

The 16 named acoustic features (8 FM + 8 AM) used for explained-variance analysis are separate from the 80D classification vector — they include freq_diff, freq_max, freq_mean, amp_max, amp_mean, and related scalar summaries
GmSLM (Sternberg et al. 2025 EMNLP) is a Mickey London + Didi Omer collaboration applying self-supervised speech models to marmoset vocalizations — a directly adjacent method to our pipeline
Omer 2025 Current Biology commentary on singing mice shows Didi is actively thinking about mouse vocalizations making the Omer lab a key potential collaborator
The Omer vectorization technique originated in this 2024 Science paper and is not referenced from an earlier publication
